gaps.explanation: Statement lines are the accrual Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Net Position - Proprietary Funds, Totals 2024 (pp9-10, printed pp14-15): Charges for services 596,224 + Lease agreement 246,399 + Miscellaneous 16 = Total operating revenues 842,639, + Interest revenue 89,220 = 931,859. The only business-type schedule is Schedule 29 'Statement of Cash Receipts and Cash Disbursements Compared to Budget' (p35, printed p69), Actual Budgetary Basis receipts: Electric 342,997 + Water 324,218 + Sewer 263,062 = 930,277 (detail lines, read correctly). Per fund: Electric 342,997 vs accrual 250,916 + 86,583 = 337,499; Water 324,218 vs 327,266 + 1,727 = 328,993; Sewer 263,062 vs 264,457 + 910 = 265,367. Budgetary receipts are cash collections (p11: receipts from customers 832,834 and interest on investments 97,443 differ from the accrual amounts). Schedule short by 1,582 because of the basis; no line missing or doubled.

Statement (pp9-10, accrual Totals 2024): Production and purchased power 53,403 + Maintenance and operation 216,510 + General 17,334 + Administrative 85,470 + Depreciation 255,932 + Interest expense 9,132 = 637,781. Schedule 29 (p35) Actual Budgetary Basis disbursements: Electric 157,156 + Water 185,053 + Sewer 327,326 = 669,535 (detail, one printed line per fund). The statement includes non-cash depreciation 255,932; the budgetary schedule counts cash outlays the accrual statement does not expense: Electric 157,156 equals the interfund '(Increase)/decrease in due to/due from (157,156)' on the p11 cash flow statement (Electric accrual expense is depreciation 86,133 only), and Water/Sewer include capital purchases (1,286 / 72,609) and principal paid (15,043 / 39,748). Printed totals 637,781 and 669,535 genuinely differ by basis (schedule above by 31,754); the one-line-per-fund schedule cannot be reconciled further.
